Sunday morning in her Andheri flat, Pooja opened the study sheet she had built in January. The Level I exam was on the second of August. Working back from it, she had set a checkpoint at the end of March: four of the ten reading blocks done.
It was the last day of March. She had finished two.
She looked at the sheet for a while, then deleted every date after March and started again from August. Six weeks of mock tests before the exam. That left fifteen weeks for eight blocks, not the ten she had planned. The spreadsheet modelling certificate she had squeezed in for May would have to go; it was nice to have, not needed.
Her colleague Deepika texted: "Still doing the modelling course with me?"
Pooja typed, "Dropping it. Exam first. Sorry 🙏" and felt her shoulders loosen.

qa.q: How many reading blocks had Pooja finished by the end of March?
qa.a: She had finished two of the ten reading blocks.

qa.q: How did Pooja feel after typing the message to Deepika?
qa.a: She felt relieved, which shows in her shoulders loosening once the extra certificate was off her plate.

qa.q: What else could Pooja do so the next checkpoint does not slip unnoticed?
qa.a: She could check progress every two weeks instead of only at month-end, so a slip shows up while there is still time to adjust.

qa.q: How might Deepika see Pooja dropping the modelling course?
qa.a: Deepika may feel a little let down at losing a study partner, but can see that the exam matters more to Pooja right now.

grounding: It shows an analyst noticing a slipped checkpoint on her exam plan, re-deriving later dates from the exam day and dropping an optional certificate.

"Fifty-eight percent," Vinita said, turning her laptop so Parveen could see the mock score. "The plan said I'd be at seventy by now."
Parveen put down her tea. "So the plan's wrong, or you are?"
"Neither. It just assumed I'd have evenings free. I've had three late closes at work this month."
"Then fix the plan."
Vinita pulled up her calendar. "Exam is the twenty-first of November. Final revision needs four weeks. Mock tests, three weeks. So all new reading must end by mid-September." She counted. "That's ten weeks. I've got four readings left, and the ESG certificate on top."
"Do you need the ESG one?"
"Not for this exam." Vinita struck through it. "It can wait till next year."
"And the seventy?"
"Checkpoint moves to the first of September. Honest date this time."

qa.q: What was Vinita feeling when she showed Parveen the mock score?
qa.a: She was probably disappointed and a little worried, since the plan said she would be at seventy by now.

qa.q: Which other change could help Vinita if late closes at work continue?
qa.a: She could protect two fixed study mornings a week, since evenings keep getting taken by work.

qa.q: How does Parveen see the slipping plan?
qa.a: Parveen treats it as a plan problem, not a personal failure, and pushes Vinita to fix the plan calmly instead of blaming herself.

grounding: It shows a young professional seeing her exam checkpoint slip, reworking later milestones from the exam date and dropping an optional certificate.
